commitResults.messageTitle: Add matriculation number and group to Person
commitResults.messageBody:
Roster identifies students by their matriculation number and organizes
them into tutorial groups, but Person only has AB3's name, phone,
email, address and tags.

Deleting a student and marking attendance both need these two fields:
the delete message names the student's matriculation number and group,
and attendance is recorded against a session of the student's group.

Let's add them as two value classes:
* Matric (m/): A, then seven digits, then one letter
* Group (grp/): one or two letters followed by two digits

Both are compulsory in the add command and are converted to uppercase,
so that, e.g., t09 and T09 are the same group. They are stored, shown
on the person card and included in command result messages. The edit
command keeps them unchanged, as editing them is not in scope yet.

The remaining Person-to-Student changes (dropping phone and address,
identifying students by matriculation number) are left to the student
model work.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add reusable model stub for command tests
commitResults.messageBody:
Command tests that need a stub model each have to define their own,
as AddCommandTest's stub is private to that test.

Let's add a shared ModelStub to testutil, in which every method fails,
so that a command test can override only the methods the command is
expected to call, and any other call to the model fails the test.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add mark command to record attendance
commitResults.messageBody:
TAs need to record whether each student was present or absent at
each weekly tutorial, but the app has no notion of tutorial sessions
or attendance.

Let's add a mark command, "mark INDEX w/WEEK s/STATUS", which records
the student at INDEX as present or absent for their group's session
in that teaching week.

To support it, let's add:
* a Session class (group, teaching week 1 to 13, date)
* a sessions list, with at most one session per group and week
* an Attendance class (session, status), held in a set by each student
* saving of sessions and attendance records to the data file

A student with no record for a session is unmarked, rather than having
a third status, so missing records are never mistaken for absences.
Loading the data file rejects records for another group's session,
more than one record for a session, or a session missing from the
sessions list.

Marking never creates a session, so a mistyped week cannot add a wrong
one; the error message tells the TA to create the session first.
Marking a student again overwrites the record, and the message names
the previous status so that an accidental overwrite is noticed. The
displayed list is left as it is, so that indexes stay the same.

There is no command to create sessions yet, so the sample data
includes sessions for the first three weeks of each sample group.
Showing attendance in the student list is left to the list feature.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test mark command against a stub model
commitResults.messageBody:
MarkCommandTest only runs the command against a real ModelManager, so
it cannot show which model methods the command calls, and a broken
filter shows up only as two unequal models.

Let's add tests that run the command against a stub model, which holds
a fixed list of students and sessions and records each replaced
student. Any other model call fails the test, including resetting the
displayed list, which mark must not do. They check that the command:
* records attendance for exactly the student at the given index
* replaces an earlier record and names the previous status
* looks the week up in each student's own group
* changes nothing when the index or the session is invalid

commitResults.messageTitle: Update delete command for students
commitResults.messageBody:
The delete command still uses AB3's wording: it reports "Deleted
person:" followed by every field of the person, and refers to persons
in its usage and error messages.

The MVP spec expects the result to name only the student, their
matriculation number and their tutorial group, and to make clear that
the student's attendance records are deleted with them.

Let's change the success message to "Deleted NAME (MATRIC) from
tutorial group GROUP, including all attendance records." and reword
the usage message and the shared invalid-index message to refer to
students.

Attendance records will be stored inside each student, so deleting the
student is enough to delete them. Tutorial groups are not removed, even
when their last student is deleted.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add reusable model stub for command tests
commitResults.messageBody:
Command tests that need a stub model each have to define their own,
as AddCommandTest's stub is private to that test.

Let's add a shared ModelStub to testutil, in which every method fails,
so that a command test can override only the methods the command is
expected to call, and any other call to the model fails the test.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test delete command against a stub model
commitResults.messageBody:
DeleteCommandTest only runs the command against a real ModelManager,
so a failure could come from the model rather than the command, and
the tests cannot show which model methods the command calls.

Let's add tests that run the command against a stub model, which shows
a fixed list of students and records each deletion. Any other model
call fails the test. They check that the command deletes exactly the
student at the given index of the displayed list, reports them by
name, matriculation number and group, and deletes nothing when the
index is out of range.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add mark command to record attendance
commitResults.messageBody:
TAs need to record whether each student was present or absent at
each weekly tutorial, but there is no way to record attendance.

Let's add a mark command, "mark INDEX w/WEEK s/STATUS", which records
the student at INDEX as present or absent for their group's session
in that teaching week.

To support it, let's add:
* an Attendance class (session, status), held in a set by each student
* a Status enum (PRESENT, ABSENT) and the s/ prefix
* saving of attendance records to the data file

A student with no record for a session is unmarked, rather than having
a third status, so missing records are never mistaken for absences.
Loading the data file rejects records for another group's session,
more than one record for a session, or a session that is not stored.

Marking never creates a session, so a mistyped week cannot add a wrong
one; the error message tells the TA to create the session first.
Marking a student again overwrites the record, and the message names
the previous status so that an accidental overwrite is noticed. The
displayed list is left as it is, so that indexes stay the same.

Sessions themselves, the w/ prefix and looking up a group's session
for a week are left to the create session feature.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject students who share an email
commitResults.messageBody:
Each student has their own email, but `add` and `edit` accept an
email that another student already uses, and so does loading a data
file.

Let's reject a student whose email matches another student's in
`add`, `edit` and when loading a data file.

Emails are compared ignoring case, as they are not case-sensitive in
practice. Changing only the case of a student's own email is still
allowed.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep every student in an existing tutorial group
commitResults.messageBody:
Every student must belong to a registered tutorial group, but nothing
ensures this at the moment.

On first launch, the sample students are in T09 and T10, but those
groups are not registered. So `session grp/T09 ...` fails with
"Tutorial group T09 does not exist" while T09's students are on
screen. `edit` can also move a student to a group that does not
exist.

Let's
* put all the sample students in T09, and register it, so that the
  sample data starts with one tutorial group
* register a student's group when loading a data file that lacks it,
  so that files saved from the sample data still load
* reject `edit` to an unregistered group, with the same message as
  `add`

commitResults.messageTitle: Show added students outside the displayed list
commitResults.messageBody:
After `init grp/T10`, or while search results are shown, `add` can
put a student in a group that is not on screen. Roster reports the
student as added, but they do not appear, so the TA cannot see or
mark them without running `list` first.

Let's show the new student's tutorial group when they would not
appear in the displayed list, and end the confirmation with "Now
showing GROUP." so that the change of view is not a surprise.

A student who belongs in the displayed list, such as one added while
viewing all students or their own group, leaves the view as it is.

commitResults.messageTitle: Scroll to and highlight a newly added student
commitResults.messageBody:
The list is sorted by matriculation number, so a new student can be
placed anywhere in it. In a long group, they are often below the part
of the list on screen, and the TA has to scroll and search for them.

Let's have `add` ask the UI to show the new student, so that the list
scrolls to their card and highlights it. The highlight is cleared by
the next command, so it never marks an unrelated student.

Cards differ in height, so a single scroll uses estimated heights and
can stop with the card partly hidden. Scrolling again after the cards
are laid out brings the whole card into view.

commitResults.messageTitle: Check and log the display of newly added students
commitResults.messageBody:
`add` now switches to the new student's group and asks the list to
scroll to them, but nothing checks that the student ends up on
screen, and asking to scroll to a student who is not displayed does
nothing silently.

Let's assert that the new student is in Roster, and that they are
displayed after their group is shown. Let's also log each add at FINE
level, log a warning when the list is asked to scroll to a student it
does not display, and reject a null student there.

commitResults.messageTitle: Keep scrolling until the added student's card is in view
commitResults.messageBody:
After `add`, the list scrolls to the new student twice: once at once,
and again on the next turn of the JavaFX event queue. The second
scroll can still run before the list has laid out its new cards, so
when the view switches groups, the card can stay almost entirely
below the visible part of the list.

Let's check after each layout of the list whether the card lies
entirely within the visible part, and scroll it into view if not,
for up to ten layouts. This no longer depends on when the layout
happens to finish.

The highlight was also kept when the next command failed, although
the User Guide says it lasts until the next command. Let's clear it
after a failed command too.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test the corrective scroll to an added student
commitResults.messageBody:
The check that scrolls an added student's card into view after layout
only acts when the first scroll leaves the card out of view, which
does not happen on every machine, so CI never runs it. `add` to an
unregistered group is not tested either.

Let's test the corrective scroll directly, by moving the list away
before it is laid out, with the card left both below and above the
visible area. Let's also test the panel when it is not in a window
yet, and `add` to an unregistered group.

The visibility check now measures against the list's scrolling area
itself instead of looking up an inner node, which removes a check
for a node that always exists once the list is shown. The helper
that waits for rendering cycles moves to FxTestUtil, as two test
classes now use it.

commitResults.messageBody: Show added students outside the displayed list

commitResults.messageTitle: Add mark all to mark every displayed student
commitResults.messageBody:
Taking attendance for a tutorial means one `mark` command per student,
so marking a group of 20 present takes 20 commands.

Let's add `mark all w/WEEK s/STATUS`, which marks every student in the
displayed list for that week. As with `mark`, each student is marked
for the session of their own group, so a list spanning several groups
still works.

The sessions of all displayed groups are looked up before anyone is
marked. If a group has no session for that week, no one is marked,
so a failed command never leaves a group half marked. The message
says how many students already had a record for that week, so that
overwriting earlier marks is visible.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add delete all to delete every displayed student
commitResults.messageBody:
Removing a whole tutorial group's students, such as at the end of a
semester, means one `delete` command per student. `clear` is faster
but also deletes every group and session.

Let's add `delete all`, which deletes every student in the displayed
list together with their attendance records. Tutorial groups and
sessions are kept, as with `delete`, so `list grp/T09` followed by
`delete all` empties T09 without removing it.

commitResults.messageTitle: Check and log the changes made by mark all and delete all
commitResults.messageBody:
`mark all` and `delete all` change many students at once, but nothing
checks that each session `mark all` uses is for the right group and
week, or that `delete all` leaves none of the deleted students
behind, and neither command logs what it changed.

Let's assert these facts, and log each command's changes at FINE
level, as the single-student commands do.

commitResults.messageTitle: Enable assertions when running the app with Gradle
commitResults.messageBody:
Java ignores assert statements unless assertions are enabled, and
`gradlew run` does not enable them. So an assertion that fails while
a developer tries out a change goes unnoticed. Tests already run with
assertions enabled, as Gradle's test task does that by default.

Let's enable assertions for the run task, as AB3 does. Users running
the JAR are unaffected, since assertions stay off there.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject students in unregistered groups in AddressBook
commitResults.messageBody:
Every student must belong to a registered tutorial group, but only
the commands enforce this. AddressBook accepts a student in any group,
while it already rejects a session for an unregistered group. Code
that skips the commands' checks, such as the tests below, can create
a student whose sessions can never be found.

Let's make addPerson and setPerson throw an IllegalArgumentException
for a student in an unregistered group, as addSession does. Four tests
added students without registering their groups; they now register
them first. Let's also reject null arguments to findSession.

commitResults.messageTitle: Assert what each Roster command and model change promises
commitResults.messageBody:
Roster's commands and model changes rely on facts that no code
checks, such as that the session found by `mark` belongs to the
student's own group, or that a student moved to another group has no
attendance records left. A later change could break one of these
without any test noticing.

Let's assert these facts where they are established:
* `init` registers the group and shows an empty list
* `session` makes the new session findable
* `mark` uses a session of the student's own group and records the
  new status
* `delete` leaves no trace of the deleted student
* `edit` leaves no attendance records on a student moved to another
  group
* `list grp/` makes the group active, and showing a group displays
  only its students
* `Person#withAttendance` leaves exactly one record for the session

The stub model in DeleteCommandTest now answers hasPerson, which the
new assertion in `delete` calls.

commitResults.messageTitle: Log changes made by Roster's commands
commitResults.messageBody:
Only AB3's own classes log anything. When a TA reports wrong data,
the log shows the commands they typed but not what each one changed,
and nothing records the two cases where Roster changes data the TA
did not ask to change.

Let's log at FINE level what `init`, `session`, `mark` and `delete`
changed, and at INFO level when
* `edit` clears the attendance records of a student moved to another
  group
* loading a data file registers a tutorial group that a student
  belongs to but the file's groups list leaves out

FINE messages are hidden unless the log level is lowered, so they add
no noise to the default log.

commitResults.messageTitle: Check undo history and log undo, rollbacks and comments
commitResults.messageBody:
The undo history keeps a list of saved states, a matching list of
command names and a pointer into them, but nothing checks that they
stay consistent. `undo` and `comment` log nothing, and when saving
fails and a change is rolled back, the log does not say so.

Let's assert, after every change to the undo history, that each saved
state has a command name and that the pointer is within the list,
and reject a null command name. Let's also log each undo and comment
change at FINE level, and log a warning when a failed save rolls a
change back.

commitResults.messageTitle: Check arguments in UI, completion and clear
commitResults.messageBody:
Some parts of Roster still trusted their callers completely. A null
or out-of-range argument there would fail later, far from its cause.

Let's,
* reject null arguments to the UI panels, cards and command box
* check the caret and replaced range in field completion
* reject a null usage or argument string in the CSV parser
* log at INFO how much data clear deletes, and assert it is empty
* assert loaded attendance records match their students' sessions

commitResults.messageTitle: Check name scoring and completion invariants
commitResults.messageBody:
Name similarity scoring and the newer completion code assume ranges
that nothing checks. A mistake there would quietly give wrong
suggestions or matches instead of failing.

Let's,
* assert name similarity scores stay between 0.0 and 1.0
* assert masking an export path keeps every character in place
* assert only a listed suggestion is scrolled into view

commitResults.messageTitle: Test range checks in field completion
commitResults.messageBody:
Field completion rejects a caret outside the text and a suggestion
with an invalid range, but no test passes such values, so the checks
could be removed or broken without any test failing.

Let's test that each of these throws an IllegalArgumentException.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge pull request #114 from My2h/branch-add-defensive-checks
commitResults.messageBody:
Add defensive checks and logging across Roster

Roster relies on facts that no code checks, and its log does not
record what each command changed.

Let's add exceptions for invalid arguments, assertions for internal
invariants, and logging of data changes, and enable assertions when
running the app with Gradle.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update UML diagrams to match v1.4
commitResults.messageBody:
The DG's diagrams describe the code as it was in v1.3. The UI diagram
lacks the group panel and attendance cells, the storage diagram lacks
sessions and attendance, the model diagram lacks comments and tags, and
the commit diagram leaves out the rollback when saving fails. Nothing
shows how attendance is marked.

Let's update those four diagrams, and add a sequence diagram for mark
and an activity diagram for mark all.

The changed class diagrams now use PlantUML's built-in smetana layout,
as the Roster model diagram already does, so they render without
Graphviz installed.

commitResults.messageTitle: Update the Developer Guide for v1.4
commitResults.messageBody:
The DG does not describe the features added in v1.4, such as mark all,
delete all, comments and field completion. Its manual testing commands
still use the phone and address prefixes, which Roster now rejects,
and its glossary describes attendance cells that no longer exist.

Let's,
* describe the new UI parts and storage records in the Design section
* explain how marking attendance works, with the new diagrams
* add sections on deleting, showing new students, comments and field
  completion
* add use cases for mark all, comments and undo
* fix the manual testing commands and add tests for the new commands
* update the glossary

commitResults.messageTitle: Update the User Guide for v1.4

commitResults.messageTitle: Open the window on screen when its saved position is not
commitResults.messageBody:
Roster reopens its window at the position saved in preferences.json.
If that position was on a monitor that is no longer connected, the
window opens out of reach, and the only fix is to delete the file by
hand.

Let's use the saved position only if the window's title bar would be
on a connected screen, wide enough to drag. Otherwise, centre the
window and log why. The title bar is what matters, because a window
the user can grab can be moved back into view.

Let's also remove this from the UG's known issues, and add a manual
test for it to the DG.

commitResults.messageTitle: Show command results in a success or error banner
commitResults.messageBody:
The result display shows every command's feedback in the same plain
text box, so a failed command looks just like a successful one. A TA
glancing up from class can miss that nothing was changed.

Let's show the feedback in a banner with a title and an icon: green
with a tick for "Command completed", and orange with "!" for "Command
not run". MainWindow now tells the display which kind of result it
is showing.

The design and code come from Yuxin's UI redesign (b0e17db4 on
87-redesign-ui). Its styles are moved from DarkTheme.css into a new
ResultDisplay.css, loaded only by ResultDisplay.fxml, so that the
other parts of the redesign can be merged without editing the same
stylesheet. Two of its rules name #resultDisplay, because the current
DarkTheme.css would otherwise draw the message box in dark grey.

Co-authored-by: yuxin <227103897+yx-0000@users.noreply.github.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Add MVP user stories to DG
Add Matric to represent matriculation numbers
Add matric and group to Person
commitResults.messageBody:
Person holds AB3's name, phone, email, address and
tags, and treats two persons with the same name as
the same person.

Roster identifies a student by their matriculation
number, and two students may share a name. A TA
cannot add two students named John Tan today,
while one student entered twice under different
names is accepted.

Let's add matric and group to Person, and identify
a student by matriculation number or email
instead of name.

Either field identifies a student on its own: both
are unique across students, so a duplicate of
either is the same student.

Callers of the constructor follow: add parses m/
and grp/, edit carries both over unchanged, and
storage reads and writes them.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge upstream/master into add-student-matric
commitResults.messageBody:
This branch adds matric and group to Person and
defines its own Group and parseGroup.

F1 has since merged a Group class, a parseGroup
that normalizes before validating, and the grp/
prefix. Keeping both copies does not compile.

Drop this branch's Group and parseGroup, and use
the ones from F1.

F1 owns tutorial groups. Its Group requires an
already uppercased code, so parseGroup is the
only safe way to build one from user input.

Test sources still do not compile; that is fixed
in the next commit.

commitResults.messageTitle: Build test sources against the new Person
commitResults.messageBody:
PersonBuilder and JsonAdaptedPersonTest still call
the five-argument Person and JsonAdaptedPerson
constructors, so the test sources do not compile.

Nothing can be run or verified until they do, not
even the tests that have nothing to do with
matriculation numbers or tutorial groups.

Give PersonBuilder a default matric and group,
with withMatric and withGroup to override them,
and pass the matric and group of BENSON through
the JsonAdaptedPerson call sites.

PersonBuilder is where almost every test gets its
people, so defaults there keep the change to one
file rather than every caller.

The suite now runs: 253 tests, 43 failing. Most
fail because every typical person shares the
default matric and so counts as a duplicate.
Fixtures and assertions follow in later commits.

commitResults.messageTitle: Identify a student by matriculation number
commitResults.messageBody:
Person identifies a student by name, and the
matriculation number and tutorial group added
earlier cannot be edited.

Two students in a tutorial group may share a
name, so a TA cannot add both. The edit command
also skips its duplicate check when the identity
field cannot change, so it can quietly create
duplicates.

Identify a student by matriculation number, and
let edit change the matriculation number and the
tutorial group.

A matriculation number is unique and stable, and
making it editable restores the check edit
already had: it compares the edited student
against the rest only when the identity changes.
All three edit tests then pass with no change to
their assertions.

Email is no longer part of a student's identity,
so two students may share one. Test fixtures gain
distinct matriculation numbers, and add and edit
command strings gain the m/ and grp/ prefixes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge upstream/master into add-student-matric
commitResults.messageBody:
This branch identifies a student by matriculation
number and adds the m/ prefix.

F2 has since merged session creation with the w/
and d/ prefixes, and F5 a new find command whose
tests build their own students.

Keep every prefix from both sides, and give the
find tests distinct matriculation numbers.

Those six students were all built from the
default, so under matriculation-number identity
they counted as one student and the roster
refused to hold them.

One find assertion expected a renamed student to
disappear, which held when identity was the name.
It now checks that the record with the old name
is gone instead.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add tests for Matric and parseMatric
commitResults.messageBody:
Matric is the only value class in model.person
with no test of its own, and ParserUtil.parseMatric
has no coverage at all.

Nothing pins the split between the two: Matric
rejects anything not already uppercased, while
parseMatric is what uppercases it. Either side
could change without a test failing.

Add MatricTest for the format rules, equality and
string form, and parseMatric cases in
ParserUtilTest for trimming and uppercasing.

The lowercase cases appear in both files on
purpose: one asserts the constructor refuses the
value, the other that the parser accepts it. Read
together they say where the boundary is.

commitResults.messageTitle: Remove phone and address from students
commitResults.messageBody:
A student carries a phone number and an address
inherited from AB3, and add requires both.

No Roster feature reads either one, and the
agreed add format is n/NAME m/MATRIC grp/GROUP
e/EMAIL. Review of #58 raised this two
iterations ago.

Delete Phone and Address, and drop the p/ and a/
prefixes from add, edit and tests.

Making them optional instead would leave fields
that nothing reads but every test fixture still
has to supply. Existing save files are
unaffected: storage ignores unknown keys, so an
addressbook.json holding phone and address still
loads.

Six tests go with the fields, two of them the
address-parsing tests from #72, which no longer
have a subject. The User Guide still documents
p/ and a/ and needs a follow-up.

commitResults.messageTitle: Drop phone and address from User guide
Add a comment field to students
commitResults.messageBody:
A student has a name, email, matriculation number,
group, tags and attendance, but nowhere to record
what a TA noticed about them.

A TA teaching three groups cannot remember who
needs following up, and the DG already carries a
user story for leaving a short note on a student.

Add a Comment value class and a comment command
that adds to, replaces, or clears a student's
note.

Notes accumulate rather than get rewritten, so c/
only ever appends and c-/ is the single prefix
that overwrites. A TA never loses a note without
having typed the prefix that means replace.

Person keeps its existing constructors, which
default the comment to empty, so no existing
caller or fixture changes.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add a name similarity scorer
commitResults.messageBody:
find matches a name by substring, so a query that
contains a typo returns nothing.

A TA who types sarh gets an empty list and no
sign that Sarah exists, and the persona in the DG
is a forgetful TA typing between tutorials.

Add a scorer that rates a query against a name
from 0 to 1, with 0.9 and above counting as a
near miss.

The measure is Jaro-Winkler rather than an edit
distance scaled by length. At four characters a
single typo costs 0.2, so sarh against Sarah
scores 0.8 and never reaches the cutoff, while
Jaro-Winkler scores that pair 0.95 and sarh
against Sandra 0.8, separating them.

Nothing calls the scorer yet. Wiring it into find
is the next iteration, so this stays a standalone
class with its own tests.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add a sequence diagram for the comment command
commitResults.messageBody:
The Developer Guide documents filtered search,
CSV export and attendance updates, but the
comment command has no section or diagram.

A reader cannot see how an append is length
checked, or that the update builds a new
Person rather than changing the stored one.

Add CommentSequenceDiagram and a Commenting on
a student section describing the command.

The diagram follows DeleteSequenceDiagram, so
it includes style.puml and groups participants
into Logic and Model boxes.

The PNG is rendered with PlantUML 1.2024.8, as
newer releases draw a warning about the
ParticipantPadding setting in style.puml.
